resolvedFindings.correction: Cancellation requires the live outer transaction, then runs locking, schema/request insertion and pre-dispatch terminal transition inside atomic. Outbox binds atomic to client.transaction(() => work()), whose transactional branch uses a same-connection savepoint and the same client/attempt state. It rolls back to and releases that savepoint before rethrowing the native statement fault.
resolvedFindings.independentNativeRegression: With a real BEFORE UPDATE OF state RAISE(ABORT) trigger firing after request insertion, the host catches delivery.claim.state, confirms pending, commits an unrelated authority row with a captured timestamp, and sees no cancellation request. Both an established request table and first-use lazy table DDL were tested. A second nested call succeeds after the caught fault; cleanup preserves the shared attempt and monotonically numbered savepoints. After trigger cleanup, claim and checkpoint succeed, demonstrating no false cancelled state or orphan request.
resolvedFindings.generatedRegressionAssessment: The fourth test supplies actual SQLite RAISE(ABORT) or PostgreSQL P0001 triggers, catches the rejected cancellation inside the outer transaction, creates a real Entry with withOperationTime configured, then checks committed Entry/pending intent/no request. Finally removes trigger/function and checks claim/checkpoint. Its intent is no partial cancellation, not preventing legitimate dispatch after failed cancellation.

safetyAssessments: The native caught-fault regression is corrected without changing the inner pre/post-dispatch decision body: reconstructed pre-correction body hashes exactly to the original pin.

The constructor closure is deferred until invocation, after client construction; it closes over the generated live transaction client rather than opening a root transaction. Nested work receives that same client, connection, policy/operation-time context and attempt state; it does not refresh the operation snapshot or reset budgets.

Nested SQLite and PostgreSQL branches await SAVEPOINT, execute work, then RELEASE on success; statement failure performs ROLLBACK TO and RELEASE before rethrow. No new autonomous transaction, commit or retry loop is introduced by cancellation.
Successful method results remain provisional until outer commit. Independent probes cover outer rollback after inner release, lazy schema rollback and cancellation inside an already nested savepoint.

Pending/retry_wait/running before possible dispatch still cancel without refunding counts, rewriting IDs/deadlines or changing the fence. Stale checkpoint/renewal reject; later same-key work is released only after committed pre-dispatch cancellation.

After possible_dispatch or consistent outcome_unknown, cancellation still inserts one idempotent database-UTC request and does not alter state, counts, lifetime, dispatch marker or FIFO block. Request-only outer rollback and both committed checkpoint/cancel orderings were exercised.

Known terminals/missing intent allocate no request; invalid ledger/marker combinations fail closed; request FK prevents orphan intent IDs. Retired transaction tokens and per-SQL callback revocation were checked.

The cancellation slice introduces no provider call, authored/public/operator endpoint, receipt assertion or service-role grant. Future golden-worker policy permission needs an owner decision separately; this review supplies none.

No independent compiler build, full gate, generated application suite, PostgreSQL test run, server, provider call or cross-process race was executed. Real SQLite primitives/native faults/savepoints were independently tested in memory; generated four-test regions were source-reviewed.
PostgreSQL savepoint branch was inspected, while actual P0001 recovery and generated authority integration are main-attributed evidence. No claim of independent PostgreSQL reproduction.

Normal acknowledged savepoint cleanup and fresh compatible compiler-owned schema are assumed. Connection loss, ambiguous commit/rollback/release, broken adapter cleanup, schema migration/drift and hostile/detached/concurrent trusted-host callbacks are not certified. Positive callback results never establish durable commit or provider rollback.

Reference-mail transition helper, acknowledge_delivery_mail, record_delivery_unknown, receipt helper and all subsequent outcome tests are excluded. Renewal remains Avicenna's review; only unchanged bytes and rejection after cancellation were observed.

This is not whole RM-306 completion, scheduler/worker binding, public cancellation authority, all golden tests, contract freeze, new owner decisions, or permission for the future golden worker's service role. Frozen ASYNC decisions and case definitions remain preserved.
